analysis: What changed vs the 6 AM brief: the open made the premarket slide real and worse. The S&P is now -3.05% and the Nasdaq -4.41% in the first 30 minutes, SPY broke below $700 within 9 minutes, and the VIX is just under 32 — the gap-down is extending, not stabilizing. Two of the three morning drivers are now confirmed rather than reported: the USTR formally unveiled the Section 301 tariff proposal (China 20% rising to 40% if the truce breaks, EU 15% rising to 20%, effective January at the earliest), and the hot PCE print (core 3.3% y/y) is doing its damage in the cash session. The AI unwind completed its round trip: Monday's +31% Huang-reinstatement rally in Nvidia is fully retraced within two sessions, and the weakness is now sector-wide and global (Kospi -6%, SoftBank -15%, every major chip name -6% or worse). Dell's -10% on a record quarter with a raised guide confirms the beat-and-fall pattern is about valuation and AI-demand durability, not results. Anthropic below its IPO price and the neocloud names breaking down show the unwind has spread from chips to the whole AI complex. Signal vs noise: the PCE overshoot, the confirmed tariff proposal, the SPY $700 break and the full retracement of the Huang rally are signal; any single-name bounce and the exact intraday percentages are noise. The risk point is the thin Thanksgiving-week tape — Thursday closed, Friday a half day — which can amplify the first move in either direction.

community_signals.takeaway: WSB sentiment is at extreme fear (~8-12/100): the community reads Monday's reinstatement rally as the biggest bull trap ever, with SPY breaking $700 as the day's defining moment. The emerging contrarian debate — 'Reddit unanimously turning bearish means the bottom is in' vs. 'everyone switching to puts is a bottom signal' — is the only pushback to the panic; community panic clearly exceeds the actual decline (SPY -2.75% vs. circuit-breaker threshold -7%).
community_signals.title: WSB Sentiment Today: SPY, QQQ, NVDA, ANT, PCE (2026-11-25) — r/wallstreetbets Daily Discussion Analysis

disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Indexes plunge in the first 30 minutes: S&P 500 -3.05%, Nasdaq Composite -4.41%, Dow -2.09% (-1,045 points). SPY broke below $700 within 9 minutes of the open, hitting an intraday low of $698.53; QQQ -4.18% at $611.45. VIX just under 32, up ~20% — above 30 signals high market stress; it hit 36 during last Friday's selloff.
headlines.why_it_matters: The post-PCE gap-down is extending, not stabilizing — the open is printing near the lows with tech leading the downside into a thin Thanksgiving-week tape.

headlines.headline: Morning data recap driving the open: October core PCE +3.3% y/y vs 3.2% expected (highest in three years; a September revision pushed the annual rate up), headline PCE 3.8% y/y as expected; Q3 GDP revised sharply higher to 4.3% vs 3.4% initially; jobless claims 189,000 vs 200,000 expected.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hot inflation plus strong growth locks in the December rate hike and keeps January in play — the Fed has no cover to blink at the selloff, and futures slid further the moment the numbers printed at 8:30 AM ET.

headlines.headline: Tariff story confirmed and detailed: the USTR unveiled proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 trading partners — China 20% (could rise to 40% if the trade truce breaks down), EU 15% (up to 20%), plus a proposed 10% tariff on aircraft hitting Brazil's Embraer. Earliest effective date January, after a public comment period; rates to be published in a Federal Register notice Wednesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: What was a WSJ single-source report at 6 AM is now an official proposal — the tariff overhang is real and multi-month, and it stacks onto the hot PCE print as a second risk-off driver.

headlines.headline: Nvidia down ~8-9% in early trading ($142.39 at 9:39 AM ET, low $141.58), third straight down day after -5.86% Tuesday — Monday's +31% Huang-reinstatement rally is now fully retraced, with Nasdaq 100 futures falling below their pre-reinstatement level before the open. Huang is set to appear next week before congressional committees over his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI unwind is the market's center of gravity — the rally that kicked off the week is gone in two sessions, and the story is now about AI capex returns and rates, not the CEO. Earnings context: Nov 17, EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B vs $109.28B expected (+103% y/y).

headlines.headline: Chips broadly crushed: SOXX -7%, Broadcom -6%, AMD, Intel, Marvell, Applied Materials and Arm each down more than 8%; memory names Micron -9% to -10.6% and SK Hynix -7%. South Korea's Kospi fell ~6% overnight and SoftBank dropped ~15%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff is sector-wide, not a single-name story — semiconductors are the epicenter and the weakness is global, with Asian chip markets leading lower overnight.

headlines.headline: Mega-caps all red in early trading: Alphabet -5.7% ($263.02, a new 52-week low), Amazon -5.7% ($237.96), Tesla -6.7% ($358.73), Meta -3.6% ($568.45), Microsoft -3.7% ($477.71); Apple the relative holdout at -1.7% ($348.05). JPMorgan cut Meta's price target to $775 from $940 on Nov 24, keeping Overweight.
headlines.why_it_matters: No mega-cap is escaping the slide and the most AI-exposed names are down most; Apple holding up best continues the rotation-into-less-AI-exposed value pattern from Tuesday.

headlines.headline: Dell down ~10% in early trading despite a record quarter: adjusted EPS $9.45 vs ~$6.59 consensus, revenue $54.94B vs $49.32B expected, full-year revenue guidance raised to $202B and AI server backlog of $132.3B. HPE down 6% after sinking 16% Tuesday; Workday, Autodesk and HP also lower after their prints.
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat-and-fall pattern is now the rule — even a record quarter with a raised guide is being sold, so the market is judging guidance, valuation and AI-demand durability, not the quarter itself.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) down ~6-7.7% to ~$75.61-$77, well below its $83 IPO price and down from the $115 high set in the opening minutes of its first trading day last Thursday; it closed below the IPO price for the first time on Tuesday. CoreWeave -10.4% (also below IPO) and Nebius -10.3%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest IPO of all time is now a proxy for the AI trade unwinding — second-tier AI names are breaking down across the board, not just the chip leaders.

Carry-forward: Q3 2026 (Nov 3) — revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M, DCF $495-505M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. WTI ~$82.75 (+0.9%) is a small tailwind for the energy complex.
